main_text.head: EXERC. XLIII.
DE ABSCESSV IN PANCREA-te, & de aorta, venaeq; causa ruptura.
main_text.p: SOlos totius substantiae morbos esse abditos ait Fernelius, nos vero tales dici mus, qui nostros latent sensus, & internas nostri corporis partes obsident. Propterea duos memorabiles, quos quidem Lugduni in duobus ægris accurate annota uimus, hic producere no abs re fuerit. Prior is autem, qui erat indigena, dives mercator, ætate virili, & ἱνσ ἀ facultates, cuius naturales suo probe fungebantur officio, veluti ex cibi, potionisq; mediocri appetentia, atq; etiam ex alui, hepatis, & venarum excrementis iudicare tum licebat. Verum de somno apud medicos duntaxat ipse coquerebatur. Cum enim dormire conabatur, tum in lipothymiam, & totius faciei frigidum sudorem incidebat. Propterea, qui tum ipsi aderant medici, ob stomachum, quem male affectum esse opinabantur, hiem Galeni propinarunt, sed fruustra, & absque ullo commodo. page.notes: Greek word after "& " (ἱνσ ἀ, rendered as printed in the scan) is partly illegible; the printed Greek is small and ambiguous, so it is given as best read. Heading lines and "muta-" hyphenated continuation at the foot follow the printed line. Ending "hie ram" is a line-break split of "hieram" as printed; "fruftra" and "se" read as printed with long s. Possible misreadings in the Greek and in the small italic words should be checked against the scan.
